real_qa.q: What is the predicted scale of charitable giving from AI company IPOs if founders and employees follow through on commitments?

real_qa.q: What annual funding threshold does Ultra Philanthropy's mid-stage fund target for organizations seeking Series A grants?
real_qa.r: Ultra Philanthropy typically enters when an organization already turns over $300,000 USD a year, though Lewers notes hearing that it can be very hard to get from $100,000 to $300,000, so they may lower that threshold. They aim to support organizations scaling from spending a few hundred thousand dollars per year to absorbing and deploying $10 million a year.

real_qa.q: How much wealth have Anthropic co-founders publicly committed to charity?
real_qa.r: Each of the co-founders of Anthropic has publicly committed 80% of their wealth to charity, though Lewers acknowledges this is not a legal lock but rather a public commitment they have made.

real_qa.q: What is Coefficient Giving's recent philanthropic commitment and its impact on effective giving funding?
real_qa.r: Coefficient Giving gave GiveWell a billion dollar commitment a couple of months ago, and GiveWell subsequently made the largest grant in its history to the Against Malaria Foundation, showing that the landscape is already changing in response to anticipated AI wealth even if IPOs never arrive.

real_qa.q: Why does Jack Lewers believe two large funders are better than one that is twice as large?
real_qa.r: Lewers states that two coefficient givings beats one that is twice as big due to concentration risk. If only one or two organizations control funding decisions, organizations working in areas less appealing to those funders or that fall outside their thematic focus could have nowhere to turn for support.

guest.bio_context: Jack Lewers studied two dead languages at Cambridge University and initially struggled to find work in mission-driven organizations. He co-founded the School of Hard Knocks charity, which uses rugby and boxing to help unemployed young men and children with behavioral issues complete their education. After eight years growing that organization from two staff to twenty, he moved to One For The World as executive director, where he worked for four years encouraging elite university graduates to donate 1% of their income to cost-effective global health causes. He founded Ultra Philanthropy in 2022 after recognizing his comparative advantage in advising ultra-high net worth donors, and now manages a mid-stage global health fund providing grants paired with technical support.
